findings.cross_file_justification: The diff introduces two arithmetic sinks in process_findings, `(( _rb > _rmax ))` and `(( _repair_wall_budget < _rmax ))`, fed by _adv_hop_charge and _adv_repair_wall_for, which are defined outside this diff. _adv_repair_wall_for reads LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS (the WARN line echoes it as the budget) and _adv_hop_charge reads cheval catalog values (headless_timeout_seconds + connect).
findings.description: Bash `(( ))` evaluates its operands as expressions, so a non-numeric string such as `x[$(cmd)]` executes `cmd`. The diff adds _conf_uint precisely to keep config scalars out of arithmetic, but the new repair-budget block compares `_rb` and `_repair_wall_budget` without applying that guard. Both values originate from a config catalog and an environment variable that this diff does not validate.
findings.failure_mode: An operator-controlled catalog entry or LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS value that is not a plain integer reaches `(( ))` and either silently evaluates to 0 (disabling the wall budget) or, if it carries `$(...)` inside an array subscript, runs arbitrary commands in the reviewer's shell.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard both values at the point of use in process_findings with the same regex _conf_uint applies (`^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,14})$`), falling back to a safe default and logging the key by name, before any `(( ))` comparison.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff splices _ADV_RUN_TAG (resolved from LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG by _adv_resolve_run_tag, not shown) into a file path that is immediately truncated with `: >` and later appended to with model-controlled JSON. Whether the tag is restricted to a safe token depends entirely on _adv_resolve_run_tag.
findings.description: The sidecar file name now embeds an environment-supplied run tag. The path is opened with `: > "$rejected_sidecar"`, which truncates whatever it names and follows symlinks, and _write_rejected_sidecar then appends the dissenter's raw payload to it. If _adv_resolve_run_tag does not reject `/`, `..`, whitespace, and empty-after-strip values, a tag such as `../../../../home/user/.bashrc` escapes the a2a directory.
findings.failure_mode: A hostile or mistyped LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG truncates an arbitrary file writable by the reviewer and fills it with model-controlled text; because stderr is suppressed and the fallback is `rejected_sidecar=""`, the damage is never reported.
findings.suggested_fix: In _adv_resolve_run_tag (or at this call site) accept only `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$`, log and drop anything else, and consider creating the sidecar with `set -o noclobber`-style or `mktemp`-in-dir semantics so a pre-existing symlink is not followed.

findings.cross_file_justification: The comment says 'the caller restores it', but the caller of _repair_diff_ok is outside the diff and cannot be verified to overwrite the repair model's id/failure_mode with the original derived values or to strip model-supplied *_derived markers.
findings.description: The mutation check now deletes `.id_derived` and `.failure_mode_derived` from both sides and treats any field the normaliser derived as free text. Two consequences follow: the repair model may rewrite a derived `id` or `failure_mode` and still pass, and it may add `id_derived: true` / `failure_mode_derived: true` to fields it actually authored without failing the comparison. Provenance of those fields then rests on code outside this diff.
findings.failure_mode: If the caller does not restore the original derived values and strip injected markers, a finding in the envelope carries repair-model text labelled as script-derived, and a model-chosen `id` can collide with or impersonate an already-used identifier after the dedup pass has run.
findings.suggested_fix: Have _repair_diff_ok (or its caller) explicitly copy `$orig.id`, `$orig.failure_mode`, and both markers back onto the accepted repair, and reject a repair whose `*_derived` keys differ from the original's.

findings.trigger_anchor: *) log "WARN: flatline_protocol.${config_key}.companion_voice='${_cv}' is not a boolean — the companion voice stays on
findings.description: A malformed `companion_voice` value defaults to on, which spawns the second-model chain and its spend. The sibling `budget_cents` path was deliberately made fail-closed in this same diff; the companion switch is the one cost-bearing toggle that still fails open.
findings.failure_mode: A typo in the config (e.g. `companion_voice: flase`) keeps paying for a second model on every run while the operator believes it is disabled.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an unrecognised value as `false` and log the warning, matching the fail-closed convention used for budget_cents.

findings.trigger_anchor: log "WARN: ${key}='${raw}' is not a whole number of at least ${floor} — ${def} applies"
findings.description: _conf_uint and the companion_voice branch echo the raw config scalar into the log unsanitised. The rest of the diff is careful to never log model text raw and to strip C1 controls from quoted values, but config scalars are not given the same treatment; a value containing newlines or ANSI escape sequences is written verbatim to stderr.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted YAML scalar injects fake log lines or terminal control sequences into the reviewer's output, which matters when logs are parsed by the chunk driver or displayed in a terminal.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the raw value through the same capped, control-stripping excerpt the diff uses for finding values (slice to ~32 chars, replace `[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]` with a space) before logging.

findings.trigger_anchor: #                             Instead of --diff-file: the script runs `git diff` on the range itself (ref names only)
findings.cross_file_justification: The diff adds the --diff-range option to the usage contract, but the parsing and the `git diff` invocation are not in the hunks shown; the documented 'ref names only' guarantee cannot be confirmed.
findings.description: A range argument handed to `git diff` without an explicit `--` separator and a leading-dash check is an option-injection sink: values such as `--output=<path>` or `--ext-diff` change git's behaviour rather than selecting a range. The comment promises ref-name-only input, so the implementation must enforce it.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated range value beginning with `-` makes git write its output to an attacker-chosen path or run an external diff driver instead of producing the review input.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the range against `^[A-Za-z0-9._/^~@{}-]+\.\.\.?[A-Za-z0-9._/^~@{}-]+$`, reject anything starting with `-`, resolve both ends with `git rev-parse --verify`, and call `git diff -- "$base" "$head"`-style with the separator present.

findings.description: _adv_record_fallback validates --sprint-id (regex plus a '..' check) and --since, but the type argument `t` is used as given to build `env="$dir/adversarial-${t}.json"`, the glob `"$dir"/adversarial-rejected-"${t}"*.jsonl`, and the run-lock key. The function's own comments say it exists because the review/audit skill agents cannot run mv themselves, so the caller is a semi-trusted LLM agent whose arguments can be influenced by repository content. A type of `*` or `rejected-*` widens the glob so every gate's sidecars are moved to .prev; a type containing `/` yields writes to unintended sibling paths. The asymmetry with the sid check suggests type validation is assumed to happen in the CLI parser, which this diff does not show.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt-injected skill invocation passes a crafted --type and the recorder moves aside or overwrites envelopes and sidecars belonging to other gates or sprints, silently changing which findings the verdict step sees.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `t` against the closed set the script supports (e.g. `case "$t" in review|audit) ;; *) error ...; return 2;; esac`) at the top of _adv_record_fallback, next to the sid check, regardless of what the arg parser does.

findings.description: The rejected_summary row is explicitly described as 'a surface of an untrusted payload' that a downstream triage agent reads one bullet per row. The clean() filter strips C0/C1 controls, zero-width and bidi format characters, but not the Unicode Tag block (U+E0000-E007F), variation selectors (U+FE00-FE0F, U+E0100-E01EF), U+061C, U+180E, or interlinear annotation characters (U+FFF9-FFFB). Tag characters in particular are invisible when rendered and are a documented vector for smuggling hidden instructions to LLMs. Model output flows into title, severity, anchor and description_head of the row with only this filter applied.
findings.failure_mode: A compromised or adversarial model response embeds Tag-encoded text in a finding title or description; the row renders clean to a human but carries hidden instructions to the LLM that consumes rejected_summary during triage.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the class to cover `︀-️`, `￹-￻`, `؜`, `᠎`, and the supplementary ranges `\U000e0000-\U000e007f` and `\U000e0100-\U000e01ef` (jq/Oniguruma accept `\x{E0000}-\x{E007F}`), or invert the policy to an allow-list of printable categories via `test("\\p{C}")` removal.

findings.description: The repair status file `_rcf` is created with mktemp, but the lock-wait sentinel is the derived path `$_rcf.lockwait`, which is removed before each hop and then created by the lock helper only when the CLI lock wait expires (up to CONF_TIMEOUT seconds later). When _ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR is unset the parent is TMPDIR or /tmp, a shared sticky directory, and the name is discoverable by listing. Another local user can pre-create the sentinel in that window to make every hop read as 'never ran' (skipping repairs and spending budget) or, on hosts with fs.protected_symlinks disabled, plant a symlink that the helper's write follows.
findings.failure_mode: A co-tenant on a shared host degrades or steers the repair phase of every review, or clobbers a file writable by the invoking user via a symlink planted at the predictable sentinel path.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the sentinel with mktemp too, or create both files inside a private directory (mktemp -d, 0700) so the sibling name is never exposed; alternatively signal lock expiry via the exit-code file already owned by this process.

findings.description: --since is validated only for the YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ shape, not for being no later than now. The age guard moves a standing envelope aside whenever its metadata.timestamp sorts before --since. A caller can therefore pass a far-future --since and force any envelope, including one a live-completed run wrote seconds ago, to be displaced and replaced by a findings: [] failure record. The comments show this path is meant to be invoked by the skill agents under a restricted allowlist, i.e. a semi-trusted caller.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt-influenced skill invocation uses `--since 2999-01-01T00:00:00Z` to retire a legitimate review envelope with findings and substitute a failure record, altering what the verdict derivation gates on.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject a --since later than the current UTC time (compare the normalized string against `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`), and consider also requiring --since to be no older than a bounded window.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff adds the arithmetic consumers of _hb in adversarial-review.sh; _adv_hop_charge and the catalog it reads headless_timeout_seconds from live outside the diff and are the source of the value.
findings.description: The new wall-budget guard evaluates `(( _est > _hb ))` and `_est=$_hb` then `(( _repair_wall_budget - _repair_wall_used < _est ))` using the value returned by _adv_hop_charge without the `^[0-9]+$` check that the sibling _last value receives. Bash `(( ))` performs expansion on its operands, so a non-numeric string of the form `a[$(cmd)]` is executed. The charge is derived from the model catalog's per-model headless_timeout_seconds, which is repo-controlled configuration. The memo parsing with `read -r _mh _mv` also silently truncates a value containing whitespace.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed or hostile catalog entry for a repair hop's timeout causes arbitrary command execution in the reviewer's shell at the point the budget guard runs, or a stray non-numeric value aborts the repair phase under set -e.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the _last guard: `[[ "$_hb" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || _hb=<fallback bound>` immediately after the _adv_hop_charge call, before memoizing or comparing it.

findings.description: _adv_lock_dir_ours accepts any directory that is a non-symlink owned by the current uid and never inspects the mode, yet the comments in _adv_lock_dir and _adv_with_cli_lock ("the directory is ours (0700, not a symlink)") treat 0700 as established. `mkdir -m 700` only applies when this script creates the directory; a pre-existing `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/loa-headless-locks-<uid>` left by an older version, another tool, or a permissive umask that is group/world-writable passes the check. Inside such a directory the per-file guard `[[ -L "$lock" || ( -e "$lock" && ! -O "$lock" ) ]]` is a check-then-use race against `exec 9>>"$lock"`, which follows symlinks and carries O_CREAT. Another local account can swap a symlink into place between the test and the open.
findings.failure_mode: On a shared host a local attacker plants a symlink named <bin>.lock in a user-owned but writable lock directory. The review then opens or creates an attacker-chosen path writable by the user (zero-byte create, flock taken on it), or the open fails and every CLI hop silently runs unserialised, defeating the KF-037 protection the lock exists for.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend _adv_lock_dir_ours to require mode 0700 (e.g. `[[ "$(stat -c %a -- "$1" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %Lp -- "$1")" == "700" ]]`), or chmod 700 and re-verify before use. After `exec 9>>"$lock"`, re-validate the opened file rather than the path: compare `stat -c %u /dev/fd/9` to `id -u` and confirm `stat -c %i /dev/fd/9` equals the inode of a fresh `lstat` of $lock that is not a symlink; fall back to _adv_run_unlocked on mismatch.

findings.description: _adv_repair_wall_for evaluates `$(( ADV_REPAIR_MAX_PER_RUN * $2 * 2 ))` with the variable raw, while _companion_post_budget guards the same variable with `_adv_num_or "${ADV_REPAIR_MAX_PER_RUN:-5}" 5`. Bash arithmetic expands variable contents recursively, so a value such as `x[$(cmd)]` is a command-substitution sink and a plain non-numeric value is an arithmetic error. The caller invokes the function with `2>/dev/null`, so the error is hidden and `wall` becomes empty, which the following `(( sum > wall + hmax ))` reads as 0 and silently collapses the repair budget. The repair timeout `$2` / `t` flows into _adv_hop_charge and _adv_repair_wall_for with the same lack of validation.
findings.failure_mode: An operator pin or a mis-set environment variable either executes embedded command substitution during budget arithmetic or silently zeroes the repair wall so the companion is reaped mid-repair, with no log line explaining why.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate ADV_REPAIR_MAX_PER_RUN and the repair timeout once where they are read, using the existing _conf_uint helper exactly as _adv_cli_hop_timeout_load does, and consume only the validated copies in every arithmetic context. Drop the `2>/dev/null` on the _adv_repair_wall_for call so a failure is visible.

findings.description: _adv_cli_hop_bound clamps only `headless_timeout_seconds` (`v`) to _ADV_CLI_HOP_CEILING. `connect_timeout` and `read_timeout` pass through _adv_pos_ceil, which admits values up to 999999999999999, and are summed into the bound unclamped (`echo $(( ct + rt ))`). That bound becomes `flock -w "$wait_s"` in _adv_with_cli_lock, the per-hop share in _companion_wait_cap, the queue budget cached in _companion_deadline_why, and therefore the global ceiling. The catalog is a repo file (`.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml` or LOA_MODEL_CONFIG), so anyone who can change repo config controls the review's wall-clock despite the ceiling the code says it enforces.
findings.failure_mode: A catalog entry such as `read_timeout: 1e15` makes a contended CLI lock wait and the companion reaper deadlines effectively infinite; the review hangs until the outer CI or operator kills it, the eight-hour-hang shape the deadline logic was added to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp `ct`, `rt`, and the final `ct + rt` to _ADV_CLI_HOP_CEILING (or a separate documented ceiling that mirrors cheval's actual clamp for those fields), and log once when a catalog value is reduced, as _adv_cli_hop_timeout_load already does for the env knob.

findings.description: The summary is meant to be an allowlist so that provider raw text (request ids, account ids, echoed headers) never reaches the tracked envelope's last_error. Two branches are broad: `catalog headless_timeout_seconds [^()]{1,100}` admits up to 100 arbitrary characters other than parentheses, and `\b[A-Z][A-Z_]{4,}\b` admits any all-caps word. `grep -vE '^REDACTED'` removes only tokens that start with REDACTED. Any identifier or secret fragment the upstream redactor misses that sits after the catalog phrase, or any upper-case org/account/env-var-like token, is copied into the committed envelope.
findings.failure_mode: A provider or adapter diagnostic that embeds an upper-case identifier or free text after the catalog note is persisted in the tracked envelope and shipped with the review artefacts, bypassing the redaction boundary the design describes.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the catalog branch to the exact shape cheval emits (numeric value plus a fixed phrase, e.g. `catalog headless_timeout_seconds [0-9._eE+-]{1,20} (not applied|clamped to [0-9]{1,6})`), and replace the generic all-caps branch with an explicit set of known cheval error tokens (PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, AUTH_FAILED, etc.).

findings.description: The test-seam guard clears _ADV_FLOCK_BIN, _ADV_PGREP_BIN, _ADV_REDACTOR_BIN and the wait/repair overrides only when no BATS marker is present. Anyone who can set the process environment re-enables every seam by exporting `BATS_VERSION=1`, after which `_ADV_FLOCK_BIN=true` turns each per-binary lock into a silent no-op and `_ADV_REDACTOR_BIN=cat` disables redaction of provider output. The seams are then used as executables (`"${_ADV_FLOCK_BIN:-flock}" -w ...`). Because environment control is operator-level in this script's normal invocation, this is a hardening note rather than a boundary bypass, but the guard offers less protection than the comment implies.
findings.failure_mode: A CI job or wrapper that inherits a stale or attacker-influenced environment with a BATS marker set runs with locking disabled and redaction replaced, without any warning line.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the seams on a single explicit opt-in that tests set deliberately (e.g. `_ADV_TEST_SEAMS=1` checked together with the BATS marker), log one WARN line whenever any seam is honoured, and restrict _ADV_*_BIN values to absolute paths under the repository's test fixtures.

findings.title: Untrusted companion metadata can delete arbitrary empty files
findings.body: `_fold_companion` trusts `.metadata.rejected_sidecar` from `companion.result.json`, accepts absolute paths, resolves relative paths under `PROJECT_ROOT`, and then runs `rm -f` on the target when it exists and is empty. A malicious or malformed companion result can set `metadata.rejected_sidecar` to an arbitrary empty file path such as a lock, sentinel, or config marker writable by the review runner, causing file deletion outside the intended sidecar area. Constrain sidecar paths to a dedicated work/output directory, reject absolute paths and `..` traversal, and avoid deleting files named by untrusted JSON.

A malicious or malformed companion result can set `metadata.rejected_sidecar` to an arbitrary empty file path such as a lock, sentinel, or config marker writable by the review runner, causing file deletion outside the intended sidecar area. Constrain sidecar paths to a dedicated work/output directory, reject absolute paths and `..` traversal, and avoid deleting files named by untrusted JSON.

findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: `metadata.rejected_sidecar` is read out of companion.result.json and used as a filesystem path with no normalization: an absolute value is used verbatim, a relative one is joined to PROJECT_ROOT without rejecting `..` components. The only guard before `rm -f` is 'regular file and zero bytes'. Empty regular files are common and meaningful (CLI lock files such as the one the surrounding comments describe, `.keep`/sentinel files, other runs' `companion.duplicate` markers, flag files). Anyone who can influence the companion envelope or write into the workdir can delete any empty file the process can reach. The check-then-delete is also a TOCTOU window.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted or corrupted companion envelope deletes an unrelated empty file, e.g. the CLI lock for another hop or run, breaking mutual exclusion or a sentinel another process relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not trust the path in the envelope. Compute the sidecar path the fold itself expects, or resolve the given value with `realpath -m` and require the result to be under the a2a rejected-sidecar directory, rejecting absolute values and any `..` segment before `rm`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The trigger is in the diff-touched .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh. The impact depends on the companion walker (elsewhere in the same script) writing companion.result.json on failure the way the primary path does; the fold already assumes primary envelopes can carry status api_failure/malformed_response, so the same must be assumed for companion envelopes.
findings.description: `comp_status` becomes `succeeded` on mere presence of a JSON object. The companion's own `metadata.status` is never inspected, even though the same jq program treats a primary envelope with `api_failure` or `malformed_response` as a failed voice. If the companion walker emits its envelope on failure (as the primary path evidently does), a companion that never produced a review is folded as a succeeded voice: its empty findings are merged, `independent` may evaluate true, `counted_as` becomes `independent_voice`, and the synthetic FAILED vq envelope that would have told the aggregator about the dropped voice is never written.
findings.failure_mode: Fail-open in a security review gate: verdict quality credits a second, independent voice that reviewed nothing, so a run with one working model reports cross-family consensus and a clean verdict.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat `($c.metadata.status // "") | IN("api_failure","malformed_response")` exactly like a missing companion.result.json and route to the failure branch (synthetic FAILED envelope, failure class). Also require `.findings | type == "array"` as part of the success test.

findings.trigger_anchor: grep -Ev 'model-invoke failed with exit code|^\[model-adapter:shim\]' | tail -1 | cut -c1-300
findings.description: The diagnostic line is cut to 300 characters BEFORE it reaches the shared redactor and the sk-/xai-/gsk_/AIza sed. Truncation can shorten a credential below the patterns' minimum lengths (`{12,}`, `{20,}`, and whatever the shared redactor requires for Bearer/URL credentials), so a partial key survives into the operator-facing stderr line. The same line is logged with no control-character stripping, so a provider error body carrying ANSI or CR sequences can rewrite or forge log lines in the operator's terminal (e.g. a fake 'Companion voice: independent' message).
findings.failure_mode: Partial API key or a forged status line lands in the stderr log that operators read to judge the run.
findings.suggested_fix: Redact first, then truncate. Strip non-printables (e.g. `tr -cd '[:print:]'`) before passing the line to `log`. Consider making the redactor's minimum-length patterns tolerant of truncated tails or redact anything after a known key prefix regardless of length.

findings.description: Only `type == "object"` is verified on the companion envelope. Under errexit+pipefail, a `cost_usd` that is a string, a `findings` value that is not an array of objects (`.value + {...}` on a non-object errors), or a non-numeric `rejected_count` makes jq fail inside an assignment and aborts the fold, taking the whole review with it instead of degrading. Separately, `companion.rc` is validated with `^[0-9]+$`, which admits `08`/`09`; `$(( rc <= 255 ? rc : 1 ))` then raises an octal 'value too great for base' error and `--argjson e ""` fails the synthetic-envelope write.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed companion envelope or rc file crashes the aggregation (review denial of service) rather than producing a degraded envelope, so the gate neither passes nor reports.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate shape in one `jq -e` (`.findings|type=="array" and (.findings|all(type=="object")) and ((.metadata.cost_usd//0)|type=="number")`) and route failures to the failed branch. Use `10#$rc` in arithmetic or tighten the rc regex to `^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,2})$`.

findings.description: An environment variable selects the executable that receives the UNREDACTED diagnostic line (the provider's raw error text, which is precisely where credentials show up). Any environment the script inherits, including CI job environments that untrusted workflow changes can influence, can point this at an arbitrary program and capture the pre-redaction text. The existing `-x` check does not constrain location or ownership.
findings.failure_mode: Pre-redaction diagnostic text, potentially containing a provider key, is handed to an attacker-chosen binary.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the override in non-test builds, or restrict it to a path under PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib owned by the invoking user; alternatively only honor it when an explicit test flag is set.

findings.title: Untrusted diff range can be interpreted as git options
findings.description: The new `_adv_range_diff` helper passes the user-controlled diff range directly to `git diff` before the pathspec terminator. If `--diff-range` is attacker-controlled, values beginning with `--` are parsed as git options, not revisions. For example, `--output=/tmp/leak` can redirect output, and `--no-index` can make git compare arbitrary filesystem paths. The trailing `--` only terminates pathspecs after the injected option has already been parsed.
findings.impact: A caller able to influence `--diff-range` can alter where review output is written or potentially cause the script to read/diff files outside the intended repository context, undermining the audit boundary.
findings.recommendation: Validate `diff_range` before calling `_adv_range_diff`: require it to resolve to allowed commit/range syntax via `_adv_range_oid` or an explicit regex, reject any value beginning with `-`, and pass only resolved commit OIDs/ranges to `git diff`.
findings.failure_mode: The new `_adv_range_diff` helper passes the user-controlled diff range directly to `git diff` before the pathspec terminator.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: `_adv_range_diff` passes the caller-supplied range straight into `git diff` as `"$2" --`. The trailing `--` only separates revisions from pathspecs; it does not stop git from parsing `$2` itself as an option. A range beginning with `-` is therefore interpreted as a `git diff` flag: `--output=<path>` writes the diff over an arbitrary file owned by the operator, `--ext-diff` re-enables the external diff driver that the preceding `--no-ext-diff` was meant to disable (and `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF` is not among the variables unset in the subshell), and `-O<file>` or `--no-index` reshape what the hunk cutter and file-list reader later parse. `_adv_range_oid` has the same shape (`"$2^{commit}"` after `--verify --quiet` with no `--end-of-options`). The value originates from the new `--diff-range` CLI argument (`diff_range` added to `main`), which in this tool is typically composed by an LLM skill from repository or sprint content, so prompt-injected content is a plausible source. The diff does not show whether `main` validates the range (e.g. resolves both sides with `_adv_range_oid` and aborts) before `_adv_range_diff` runs, so this is rated as a defense-in-depth gap rather than a confirmed exploit.
findings.failure_mode: A `--diff-range` such as `--output=/home/u/.gitconfig` (or `--ext-diff` with a hostile `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`) is accepted by `git diff`, clobbering an operator-owned file or executing a configured external command instead of producing the reviewed-tree diff; the review then proceeds on an empty or attacker-shaped diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Diff on the two resolved commit OIDs from `_ADV_RANGE_OIDS` (hex-only, `base..head`) rather than the raw range string, and insert `--end-of-options` immediately before the revision argument in both `_adv_range_diff` and `_adv_range_oid` (git >= 2.24). Reject any `--diff-range` value whose first character is `-` in `main`. Also add `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF` to the variables unset in the subshell.

findings.description: `_adv_kill_tree` sends STOP, the requested signal (TERM or KILL) and CONT to every pid collected by `_adv_tree_pids` without checking the start token; only the later KILL in `_adv_kill_same` is identity-gated. A collected descendant that exits between the `pgrep`/`ps` walk and the first `kill -STOP` pass frees its pid, and an unrelated same-user process that receives that pid is then frozen and TERMed. Because the pid=token pairs are taken after the freeze, the token recorded for such a recycled pid describes the new process, so `_adv_reap_primary` (which has no pre-freeze token read, unlike `_adv_reap_companion_inner`) will also KILL it after the grace period. Separately, `_adv_is_same` treats an empty token as 'the pid alone decides', so on a host where `_adv_proc_start` fails (e.g. no `ps`, as the pgrep-less fallback anticipates) every KILL is sent on the bare pid.
findings.failure_mode: A reap under heavy load or on a host with fast pid wraparound stops, terminates or kills an unrelated process owned by the operator (another editor, shell, or a concurrent `claude -p`), not just the companion tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Read start tokens for the collected pids BEFORE the first STOP pass and only signal pids whose token still matches at signalling time; in `_adv_reap_primary` take a pre-freeze token read like `_adv_reap_companion_inner` does and prefer it over the post-freeze one. When `_adv_proc_start` is unavailable, skip the KILL escalation (log and leave the pid) rather than killing on pid alone.

findings.description: When `setsid` is present the watchdog handle stored in `_ADV_CONT_WD` is a negative value (`-$!`), and `_adv_kill_tree` later runs `kill -KILL -- -<pgid>`. If the watchdog has already fired and exited (its delay defaults to 10 s, and the two freeze/collect passes between fork and cancel are not bounded), the process-group id can be reused by a new session leader, and the group KILL lands on an unrelated process group of the same user. The non-setsid fallback puts the watchdog in the reviewer's own group, so a group KILL of the reviewer also kills the watchdog and leaves the frozen `claude -p` tree stopped indefinitely, holding its per-binary lock.
findings.failure_mode: Under load, a cancel issued after the watchdog's delay has elapsed KILLs a recycled process group; without `setsid`, a reaper killed mid-freeze leaves the companion tree permanently stopped (lock held until manual intervention).
findings.suggested_fix: Before the group KILL, verify the watchdog is still alive and still ours (e.g. `kill -0` plus a start-token check on the stored pid, or have the watchdog write its own pid+token to a file in the workdir). Consider using `kill -KILL "$pid"` on the setsid child itself rather than the group, since `sh -c` with a single `sleep` child can be handled by also killing the sleep pid; and in the non-setsid fallback use `nohup`/`setsid -f` alternatives or document that the freeze-forever failure mode exists.

findings.description: The new --record-fallback branch exits main right after the sprint-id emptiness check. It runs before config load, before the CONF_ENABLED gate, before _adv_take_run_lock, and before the envelope move-aside logic. The caller supplies status, reason and since verbatim. Nothing in the diff restricts the status to a failure class, and --since is optional, so a record written without it displaces whatever envelope stands at the path, including a fresh one from a completed run. The script's own comments treat the invoking skill as the adversary (a skill granted `git diff *`), and this branch hands that skill a write to the gate record that skips every control the review path enforces, with no lock held.
findings.failure_mode: A skill that wants to avoid or overwrite an adversarial review calls --record-fallback <status> with no --since. If _adv_record_fallback accepts any status the downstream verdict reads as non-blocking, the gate is bypassed without a model call. Even with a failure-only status set, the record can clobber a concurrent run's envelope because the run lock is never taken, and an unvalidated --since string can defeat the newer-envelope guard if the comparison is lexical.
findings.suggested_fix: Take the run lock, or refuse while it is held, before writing the record. Whitelist the status to failure-class values the verdict treats as blocking. Require --since whenever an envelope already stands at the path and reject anything that is not a strict ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Apply the same sprint-id shape check the review path relies on before this branch.

findings.description: sprint_id is only checked for emptiness in main, yet the diff interpolates it into several new filesystem sinks: the mktemp -d template, the lock directory passed to _adv_take_run_lock, both sidecar paths, the envelope path handed to _adv_move_aside, and the record path inside the --record-fallback branch. _run_tag from _adv_resolve_run_tag is spliced into the sidecar names with no visible shape check either. A value containing / or .. redirects the lock, the rename and the workdir outside grimoires/loa/a2a/. The rename is the sink that matters: _adv_move_aside renames <path>/adversarial-<type>.json to .prev wherever the traversal points.
findings.failure_mode: --sprint-id '../../../other/dir' makes the run rename a file named adversarial-review.json in an arbitrary directory the user can write, create a lock there, and create the workdir under an unexpected parent. If a loader not shown in this hunk already validates the shape, this drops to LOW.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate sprint_id and the run tag against ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ immediately after the emptiness check and before the --record-fallback branch. Reject .. and / explicitly so every downstream path builder can trust the component.

findings.description: The --diff-range block installs `trap 'command rm -f -- "$_ADV_RANGE_DIFF"' EXIT` to remove the generated diff. The workdir block later installs `trap '_adv_cleanup_on_exit' EXIT`, and bash replaces rather than chains EXIT traps. Unless _adv_cleanup_on_exit also removes _ADV_RANGE_DIFF, every range run leaves the full diff of the reviewed commits under TMPDIR after exit. mktemp creates it 0600, so exposure is limited to the same user and root, but the diff can carry secrets committed in the range.
findings.failure_mode: Diffs accumulate under /tmp across runs on a long-lived or shared host. Any process running as the same user, or a later --diff-file pointed at a stale file, reads commit content the run was supposed to discard.
findings.suggested_fix: Have _adv_cleanup_on_exit remove ${_ADV_RANGE_DIFF:-} as well, or create the range diff inside the workdir after the workdir exists so one trap covers both.

findings.description: The two sides of the range are resolved to commit OIDs before the diff so metadata.scope pins what was reviewed. When _adv_range_oid fails for either side, or returns something outside the hex shape, the code silently falls back to _rr="$diff_range" and diffs by ref name, leaving _ADV_RANGE_OIDS empty. The scope then names only moving refs. The comments say a skill refused by the run lock adopts the standing envelope when the scope matches, so an unpinned scope can match a later run that reviewed different commits under the same ref names. The diff sha256 in scope mitigates this only if the adopter compares it.
findings.failure_mode: A review of main...feature recorded with ref names only is adopted for a later main...feature after feature moved, if the adopter matches on range text rather than OIDs or hash.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an OID resolution failure as a refusal, the same way a failed diff is, instead of falling back to ref names. Emit a diff_range_failed refusal with the unresolved side named.

findings.anchor: result=$(echo "$result" | jq --arg e "${_vq_err:-aggregator returned no output}" '.metadata.verdict_quality_error = $e')
findings.description: The last non-blank stderr line of the Python aggregator, up to 240 characters, is copied into the envelope under metadata.verdict_quality_error. The envelope is written under grimoires/loa/a2a/, a repository path that is likely committed. Python exception text routinely includes absolute paths under TMPDIR and the home directory, and may echo field values from the sidecars it parsed, some of which derive from model output.
findings.failure_mode: Local filesystem layout or model-authored text lands in a committed artefact that other tooling reads as trusted metadata.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a fixed error class on the envelope and keep the raw stderr line in the run log only, or strip absolute paths before recording it.

findings.title: Empty explicit --envelope falls back to default sibling instead of failing closed
findings.description: The new rejected-payload contract documents that a missing explicit --envelope path is a usage error, but the parser accepts `--envelope ""`, records a warning, and later silently falls back to `$(dirname -- "$FILE")/adversarial-${GATE}.json`. In automation where the envelope path is assembled from an upstream variable, an empty value can cause the validator to check the wrong envelope and miss rejected dissent payloads that should block the gate. This is a security-control bypass for the review/audit validation layer, though it requires control over the validator invocation or a caller bug that produces an empty path.
