findings.description: The diff adds gh_title_renders_raw so a --title cannot carry Markdown that changes how the heading renders (`<!` and `<[A-Za-z/!?]` are refused, among others), and adds a ledger lint whose stated invariant is that every Index link resolves to a rendered heading. But the two values op_new and op_notes_header write as FREE-STANDING lines — --reading-guide and --note — get only san1, which trims leading whitespace and so places the value at column 0. A value of ``` or ~~~ opens a fenced block, and a value of <!-- opens a CommonMark type-2 HTML block that ends only at a later line containing -->. Since a new entry is appended at the end of the file, every entry written afterwards sits inside that block: on GitHub its `## KF-NNN:` heading is not a heading, its anchor does not exist, and the Evidence rows are invisible. The new lint skips fenced blocks (so a ``` reading guide would at least fail CI) but does not model HTML blocks, so the <!-- variant passes the lint, passes verify_and_swap (grep still sees the headings) and passes kf-auto-link.py-style `^##\s+KF-` readers, while hiding the ledger from human readers on GitHub — the exact anti-tamper property the file header says this helper exists to protect.
findings.failure_mode: A single kf-write new --reading-guide '<!--' (or notes-header --note '<!--') call by the automation that is supposed to be constrained by this helper renders all later known-failures entries invisible on GitHub without tripping the writer's guards or the new link lint.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate free-standing values the way titles are now gated: refuse (or prefix with inline text so they are never at column 0) any --reading-guide/--note value matching a CommonMark block starter at line start — ^ {0,3}(```|~~~|<!--|<\?|<![A-Z]|<[A-Za-z]|#{1,6}( |$)|[-*+] |[0-9]{1,9}[.)] |>|\||[-*_]{3,}\s*$). Teach _kf_link_lint to skip HTML blocks (type 1 and 2 at minimum: lines from `<!--` to a line containing `-->`, and `<pre|<script|<style|<textarea` to their closing tag) exactly as it skips fences, so the shipped-ledger test detects a hidden tail.

findings.description: Twenty suites now export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR to BATS_TEST_TMPDIR so the CLI's per-user lock is never contended with a live adversarial-review run. The lock exists to serialize access to shared operator state (.run/ ledgers, a2a sidecars). Bypassing it is only safe when every resource the lock guards is also redirected. adversarial-review.bats and adversarial-review-e2e.bats redirect both ledger paths; the other eighteen suites (bug-809, cycle-109-*, cycle-124, cycle-baseline-capture, model-adapter-probe-integration, wire-schemas-api-safe, input-size-consumers, butterfreezone, spiral-harness, kf-011-debug, degraded-on-rejection, hallucination-filter, ledger-isolation-discovery) only redirect the lock. Any of them that execs the CLI in a mode that writes shared state can now interleave with a concurrent live run instead of blocking on it. Separately, bats creates BATS_TEST_TMPDIR with mkdir under a 0700 run dir, so the test dir itself is typically 0755. If the CLI validates XDG_RUNTIME_DIR per the XDG spec (owner, mode 0700) and falls back on rejection, the override silently resolves to the shared lock path and the isolation the comments promise does not happen. The new e3 lint checks only that no suite uses a mktemp fallback for XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; it does not check that a suite overriding the lock also redirects the state the lock protects.
findings.failure_mode: A suite that overrides the lock dir but not every shared path the lock serializes writes into the operator's live ledgers or sidecars concurrently with a real dissent run, corrupting them; or the CLI rejects the non-0700 dir and quietly falls back to the shared lock, so tests block on or steal a live run's lock despite the override.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the e3 lint in tests/unit/adversarial-review.bats so any suite exporting XDG_RUNTIME_DIR must also export LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH and LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH, or appear in ledger-isolation-discovery's covered list. In the shared setup, chmod 700 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" after exporting it. In the CLI, fail loudly when the resolved lock dir does not meet its ownership and mode checks instead of falling back to a shared path, so a misconfigured override is visible in test output.

findings.cross_file_justification: The gate change in config.ts is consumed by executeMultiModelReview in core/multi-model-pipeline.ts, which now constructs a ChevalDelegateAdapter for a keyless entry. That adapter spawns a local CLI that authenticates with whatever credentials are cached on the host (OAuth login, keychain). Whether an untrusted party can select the headless voice depends on how multiModel.models is populated; BridgebuilderConfig exposes repoOverridePath, which suggests per-repo overrides may feed this field.
findings.description: Before this change the environment was the sole opt-in for a provider: no API key in process.env meant no dispatch, in both graceful and strict modes. After this change a config entry whose model_id is a registry headless alias (claude-headless, codex-headless, gemini-headless) is dispatched with no environment opt-in at all, routing the PR diff and prompt through the operator's ambient CLI credentials. The allowlist is tight (exact case-sensitive registry key, provider pairing, unknown providers still rejected), so this is not an arbitrary bypass, but it does shift the trust boundary from 'operator provisioned a key' to 'config names a headless id'. If multiModel.models can be set or overridden from a reviewed repository, a PR author can cause the reviewer host to consume the operator's personal quota and have usage attributed to the operator's identity rather than a service key. The strict api_key_mode, which operators may rely on as a fail-fast, now passes silently for headless entries.
findings.failure_mode: A reviewed repository or a shared config supplies a headless model id. On a host where the operator deliberately did not provision an API key for that provider, the review still runs and bills against the operator's personal CLI login. In strict mode no error is raised, so the operator has no signal that a provider they did not opt into was engaged.
findings.suggested_fix: Require an explicit environment opt-in for headless dispatch, for example an allow-list env var such as BB_HEADLESS_PROVIDERS=anthropic,openai that validateApiKeys consults alongside the registry check. Alternatively, only honor headless entries from the operator-owned top-level config and reject them when they originate from a repo override. Log at warn level whenever a voice is dispatched via the headless path so the credential source is visible in run output.

findings.cross_file_justification: The empty string is passed into createAdapter in adapters/adapter-factory.ts and on to ChevalDelegateAdapter in adapters/cheval-delegate.ts, neither of which is in the diff. Whether an empty key is forwarded into the child CLI environment or into any direct HTTP path cannot be confirmed from the diff.
findings.description: The previous code enforced an invariant that createAdapter always received a non-empty apiKey because keyless entries were skipped with continue. The new code passes an empty string for headless entries. If the cheval adapter sets the provider env var unconditionally (for example env: { ...process.env, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: apiKey }), the child CLI will see an empty key, which some CLIs prefer over their cached login and will then fail or behave unexpectedly. If adapter-factory ever selects a non-cheval adapter for a provider, an empty key would produce an unauthenticated API request. The new test multi-model-headless-key.test.ts mocks generateReview on the prototype and only inspects this.opts.model, so it does not assert what apiKey value the adapter was constructed with.
findings.failure_mode: A headless voice is constructed with apiKey set to an empty string. The adapter forwards it into the child environment, shadowing the CLI's own authentication and causing the hop to fail, or a non-cheval adapter path sends a request with an empty bearer token.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass undefined rather than an empty string for headless entries and have the adapter omit the env var when the key is falsy. Extend the headless test to capture the createAdapter arguments (or the adapter constructor opts) and assert that no key is forwarded for the headless route.
